page: Amazon Web Services m5a.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower-to-average tiers. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng falls in the bottom 10%, while PassMark CPU and encryption tests show average performance in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests indicate weak read and write speeds, placing in the bottom 25%. For specialized tasks, the instance achieves average text generation speeds on small 135M LLM models, but drops to the bottom 10% for medium 7B models. Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput also rank in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m5a.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, making it a viable option for workloads that require moderate memory allocations without demanding high-performance compute capabilities. Given its benchmark profile, the instance is suited for general-purpose workloads such as basic web serving, small-scale database operations, development environments, and lightweight background processing tasks that do not rely heavily on high-speed sequential memory access or intensive mathematical computation.
